text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

-- Zaklad Energetyczny Zamosc SA signed an agreement with U.S. company Southern Electric International forming a venture which will next year start building a gas-fired electrical heating plant. The $80 million project will be completed in 1999.

-- The consolidation of a banking group around Pekao SA will take several years and it is unclear when it will be completed or how much it will cost. Unifying the computer systems will alone require about $100 million.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
-- A survey by Demoskop shows that consumer confidence declined markedly in October.
-- Four parliamentary committees will recommmend that the lower house pass a bill liberalising abortion which was rejected by the senate.
-- Volkswagen's Poznan plant will begin assembly of a three-door Polo model this year.

-- A plan prepared by Price Waterhouse and the communications ministry for expansion of rural telephone services envisages charging a general levy on all telephone users for the Telecommunications Development Fund.

-- Managers of PEPEES SA in Lomza, a food and brewery company under National Investment Fund 3, plan to submit an issue prospectus to the Securities Commission this year. The firm aims to enter the main floor of the Warsaw Stock Exchange through a public sale of all shares issued so far.
NOWA EUROPA
-- Electrical equipment maker Apator Torun aims to float 1.3 million to 1.4 million of its shares on the stock exchange in January next year.
-- More than half a million series A shares of food producer Pekpol SA will probably enter public trading this year, its President Jerzy Grudzinski said.
ZYCIE WARSZAWY

-- Justice Minister Leszek Kubicki said he would delay any decision on his resignation until after the the 1997 budget was passed. He is displeased over the small amount of funds allocated for the justice system.
PARKIET
-- The Warsaw Stock Exchange, following Western examples, has started selling information and plans to derive 15 percent of its revenue from this business.
-- KrakChemia retailer plans to invest 30 million zlotys over the next two years in two supermarkets, Dom-Hobby-Ogrod in Krakow and Laura in Tarnow.

-- Kredyt Bank shareholders, at an extraordinary general meeting on October 23, will decide whether to increase the company's share capital through an issue of series M and N shares which will be offered to the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
